title: RBAC core: effective-permission resolution engine and declarative route permission guard
objective: Port the effective-permission model: a pure, unit-tested resolution module (union of direct + role + group-role + group-direct grants within tenant context, global grants for Internal scope) plus repository lookups and a declarative requirePermission route guard reproducing the .NET RequirePermission semantics (P-03, M-05, spec 13 AuthZ).
scope: domains/rbac/effective-permissions.ts: pure function computing the effective permission set from typed grant inputs (direct user permissions, user roles, group memberships with group roles and group direct permissions), scoped per tenant with global/Internal handling
domains/rbac/repository.ts: Kysely lookups fetching a user's grant inputs for a tenant (and global) efficiently (no N+1; single round-trip or few)
lib/auth/require-permission.ts: route middleware factory requirePermission('permission.key') evaluated against the resolved effective set; 403 problem+json without leakage
Visibility-breadth permission support surfaced as a queryable capability (e.g., leads.view_all) for later query-filter enforcement (P-03/P-08)
Caching discipline: per-request resolution only (no cross-request in-memory caching for correctness, N-02)
out_of_scope: Tenant-context middleware (T-013) — the guard composes with it
implementation_details: Pure module signature: computeEffectivePermissions(input: GrantGraph, scope: { tenantId?: bigint, global: boolean }): Set<PermissionKey> — port .NET unit-test cases verbatim as the behavioral contract.
Global-permission session model parity: zero-membership Internal users must still resolve global grants (prior-build T-045 behavior).
requirePermission attaches required-permission metadata to the route for auditability/testing; composes after authenticate() and (for tenant routes) after tenant middleware so tenant scope is known.
Effective-access read model for the User Manager effective-access view reuses the same pure module (single source of truth).
Permission keys referenced in code must exist in the T-006 catalog — add a convention test cross-checking route-required keys against the seeded catalog.

unit: Effective-permission union across all grant paths (direct, role, group-role, group-direct); tenant-scoped vs global; deactivated grants excluded; empty-grant users resolve to empty set; Internal zero-membership global resolution
Ported .NET effective-permission test cases pass unchanged in expectation
integration: requirePermission on a test route: user with grant passes; without grant gets 403 problem+json; anonymous gets 401
Grant-graph lookup returns correct inputs from seeded fixture data without N+1 (query-count assertion or single-query design review)
Route-required permission keys all exist in the seeded catalog
e2e: Role-403 sweep parity covered in T-043

RBAC core implemented: pure effective-permissions module, single-round-trip Kysely repository, requirePermission() guard mounted after auth/tenant. .NET semantics MEASURED with citations: RequirePermissionFilter.cs 401 for no subject (:35-38), 401 for missing users row OR !IsActive (:40-44), 403 ONLY for a resolved active user lacking the permission (:51-54), detail strings verbatim (:63,:69), pinned by RequirePermissionTests.cs:49/69/90/109. EffectivePermissionResolver.cs unions four paths (:71-75) with per-hop predicate (TenantId == null || == tenantId); role path checks BOTH user_roles.tenant_id and roles.tenant_id plus is_active (:39-47); group-role checks group AND role scope (:49-60); group-direct checks group scope only (:62-69). Confirmed asymmetries are deliberate: user_permissions has no is_active column, group_members is not tenant-scoped. AMBIGUITY FLAGGED AND RESOLVED: the reference memoises per request (EffectivePermissionResolverTests.cs:173-193 asserts Assert.Same, i.e. a revoked grant stays effective for the rest of that request) - reproduced WITHIN a request while N-02 forbids it across requests, achieved by creating the memo inside the request closure. DELIBERATE DEPARTURE: repository loads the grant graph UNFILTERED with scopes/active flags attached and the pure module applies the predicate - filtering in SQL as the reference does would have reduced the 'pure module' to a one-line union whose unit tests could not fail. pathScopes is a LIST because a group-assigned role must satisfy group AND role scope; collapsing it would silently widen access (test: 'requires EVERY hop'). forTenant() deliberately unused here: it emits tenant_id = $1 while every predicate is 'is null or = $1', so using it would drop every global grant. Single round trip proven via Kysely log hook asserting executed.length===1 plus 3 union alls, with a second test adding 3 roles + 3 groups that the N+1 shape would fail, both carrying positive controls. Visibility breadth exposed as EffectiveAccess.canViewAll(domain) -> boolean threaded into repository functions, mirroring the reference's callerHasViewAll rather than passing EffectiveAccess itself (which would let a store invent its own rule). 10 mutants all red, with positive controls throughout so blanket denial cannot pass. REAL BUG CAUGHT BY ITS OWN TESTS: a raw pg.Pool bypassed poolerPoolConfig's int8 parser, so tenant_id arrived as a STRING and every === comparison was false - failing CLOSED (tenant-scoped grants denied, global grants unaffected), a permissions-shaped symptom with a driver-config cause; fixed by using the project pool config and pinned by a test asserting scopes are numbers. Orchestrator verified after both parallel tasks settled: 42 files / 655 tests / 0 skipped, typecheck 0, lint 0, and T-010's ci:test skip gate exit 0 (655 >= floor 595, 0 skipped).

Evaluator verdict: PASS. .NET semantics spot-checked against the cited lines by the evaluator (RequirePermissionFilter.cs:35-38/40-44/51-54/63/69; EffectivePermissionResolver.cs:35-75): role path checks BOTH user_roles.tenant_id AND roles.tenant_id plus r.IsActive; group-role checks group scope+active AND role scope+active; group-direct group-only; direct has no active flag; group_members confirmed not tenant-scoped (migration 20260718001200_rbac.sql:101-110 has no tenant_id). RULING - architectural departure RATIFIED: loading the graph unfiltered and applying the per-hop predicate (scope == null || scope == tenantId) in the pure module is behaviour-identical to the reference SQL filtering in every case incl. tenantId=null (EF null-compensation makes x.TenantId == tenantId with a null parameter equal IS NULL, exactly scope === null here); UNION ALL + Set dedup equals EF Union; verified over real rows by rbac-repository.test.ts (13 tests) and the unit matrix (24 tests). RULING - per-request memo VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, both halves: within-request memo matches the reference (double-guard route resolves in exactly 1 query, mirroring EffectivePermissionResolverTests.cs:173-193 Assert.Same), and nothing survives across requests (revoke-between-requests test asserts 403 + a 2nd query). Evaluator mutants, all restored byte-identical (sha256 verified): (A) scopeApplies -> return true failed 5/24 unit tests; (B) memo hoisted out of the request closure to factory scope failed exactly 're-resolves permissions on every request (no cross-request cache, N-02)' (1/14). Single round trip re-verified via the Kysely log hook (executed.length===1 + three UNION ALLs, incl. the 3-role/3-group case the N+1 shape fails). int8-string driver bug fix confirmed pinned by 'returns tenant scopes as numbers, not bigint strings'. Security: fail-closed 500 when permissionResolution is unmounted (tested); 403 detail verbatim with no resource data (asserted, incl. no-permission-oracle body check); caller permission set never logged (asserted).
